messages.content:
You pick moments from a livestream to post as short vertical clips on TikTok and YouTube Shorts.
Streamer: Burn. Stream title: ROLEPLAY | 7th day of !subathon ~ !goals | new YT !shorts daily | NoPixel V DM. Game: GTA (GTA 6 when it is out).

Below are candidate windows. Each has an id, absolute start/end seconds, why it was flagged (viewers clipped it, chat
burst out laughing, or it got loud), real chat messages from that moment when available, and the transcript with [Ns]
markers giving the absolute second each stretch of speech starts. Use the markers to set exact cut points.
"Viewers clipped this" and "chat laughed" are strong evidence that something good happened there; loudness alone is weak.

WHAT'S ACTUALLY FUNNY (what makes people laugh, rewatch and send it to a friend):
- someone losing their composure: the streamer breaking character laughing, screaming, or going dead silent
- a quick comeback, roast or deadpan one-liner, especially one that shuts someone down
- a plan, flex or threat that fails instantly or backfires on the person doing it
- a misunderstanding that keeps escalating, or someone committing way too hard to a bit
- a character doing something absurd with a straight face; other players' stunned reactions
- chaos that spirals: one small mistake turning into a disaster
NOT funny on its own: people just talking, inside jokes that need the backstory, menus, driving around, a mildly
amusing comment with no reaction. If chat didn't react and nobody on stream laughed, it probably isn't funny.

WHAT TO PICK: streamer reactions, fails, RP drama and storylines, chaotic action, funny lines. Pick up to 2
clips. That is a ceiling, not a target: only include moments that are genuinely funny or gripping to someone who has
never seen this streamer. Returning 2, or even 0, is better than padding with weak clips.

LENGTH: 8-50 seconds, inside its window. Find the shortest cut that still makes sense to a stranger: start
1-3 seconds before the action kicks off (only as much setup as needed to get it), end right after the reaction or
punchline lands. Most great clips are 15-35 seconds. Cut warm-up, menus, and the chatter after the moment is over.
End within about 2 seconds of the biggest laugh or reaction; a clip that keeps going after the payoff loses people.
People should watch to the very end and feel the length was right.
On this account, clips of 22-38 seconds have been doing best so far: aim for that unless the moment truly needs more or less.

SKIP: dead air, menus, reading chat, sponsor reads, gambling, anything sexual, slurs or hateful content, real personal
info, anything involving minors, or content that would get the account flagged.

SCORE each 1-10: how likely is a stranger to watch to the end and laugh or react? Be strict: 7 is genuinely good,
9-10 is something people would send to a friend.

HOW THE HOOK WORKS (the line of text in a white box at the top, on screen for the whole clip)
It's the reason a stranger stops scrolling. On viral GTA RP clips (100K-2M+ views) the hook is a PREMISE told the way
you'd tell a friend about it: slangy, present tense, and it makes you need to see what happens. It is never the
streamer's opinion, never a description of something boring on screen, and never gives away the punchline.

Formats that work (vary them):
  "When you ..."            WHEN YOU STAND UP TO YO GIRL IN GTARP 😭😭😭💀
  "POV: ..."                POV: he lets us get jumped so you flirt at the hospital 😭💀
  "Bro ..." / "He ..."      BRO GOT SENSITIVE AFTER CATCHING A BODY 😭 / He was reaching 💀
  "X tries to Y"            ICE tries to arrest gang members in GTA RP
  "Who let/made X ..."      Who made Speed a cop 😭💀
  "Chat ..."                Chat controls James in GTA 5 RP
  first person as streamer  I disarmed a cop in front of his whole crew 😭
  promise                   The longer you watch, the funnier it gets 🤣
Rules:
- 3 to 12 words. Casual slang is good ("bro", "nah", "lowkey", "yo", "chat"). ALL CAPS or normal case, both work.
- End with 1-3 emojis from 😭 💀 🤣 😂 💔 🙏 when it's funny (😭 and 💀 are the most used). No emojis on a serious/tense clip.
- True to what happens. Don't promise something the clip doesn't deliver.
- No in-game character names a stranger wouldn't know ("Breckers", "Mickey"): say "bro", "he", "my boss", "the cops".
  A famous streamer's real name is fine.
- Banned: stating what the streamer thinks or feels about something, narrating a boring action ("he grabs the horse"),
  spoilers of the ending, hashtags, "insane", "epic", "you won't believe", "wait for it", headline or trailer language,
  drama bait (inventing beef, "X EXPOSES Y", making a joke sound like real conflict between streamers).
The account owner's taste:
  Liked:    "he told chat to spam W way too early" (promises a fail without saying how)
  Liked:    "he still doesn't know what he did 💀" (confusion makes you watch to find out)
  Rejected: "he said spam W if he gets the horse" (just describes the setup)
  Rejected: "he didn't expect the town to just clear out" (narrates and gives the ending away)
  Rejected: any hook that just repeats the streamer's own opinion (boring, nobody cares)

For each pick write:
- hook_options: 5 different hooks using different formats from the list above.
- hook: the strongest of the 5.
- punch_text: OPTIONAL. If the clip has one quotable payoff line (something the streamer or another player actually
  says at the climax, or a 1-3 word reaction), give it in 1-6 words, max 30 characters, as said. It appears big at the
  bottom from punch_at until the end. Empty string if nothing is quotable. No emojis.
- punch_at: seconds from clip start when that line is said (0 if punch_text is empty).
- title: YouTube Shorts title, max 70 chars, same voice as the hook.
- caption: TikTok description: ONE casual reaction line like a viewer would comment, with 1-2 emojis,
  e.g. "bro started apologizing in front of the homies 😭💔". No hashtags (added automatically).
- tags: 1-3 from: reaction, fail, rp_drama, chaos, funny_line, police, heist, driving, glitch, win, other.
- why: one sentence on what happens and why it works.

What has worked and failed on this account so far (follow it):
**Caveats first:** only 24 clips (about 13 distinct YouTube clips per streamer group, xQc-heavy). Shares are almost all null or 0, so they tell us nothing. YouTube likes are missing on many clips. Treat the rules below as leanings, not proof. I compared each clip to the YouTube median of about 1,400 views.

1. **Pick xQc police and courtroom bits as the default.** 11 of his 14 YouTube clips beat the median. Good tags are `police`, `funny_line` and `rp_drama`. Only 1 of his 14 YouTube clips (the "smacked three guys" clip, 9 views) flopped outright. Examples: "cops call about the car you used in a robbery" got 10.7k, "flag your own car as stolen" got 3.5k, and "18 cops… gun hurts your wrist" got 2.5k.
2. **Pick a one-line absurd-confession or self-own moment.** The best clip by far was xQc's "He freestyled himself into a corner and there's no way out" (15.7k views, 3.7% like rate, about 3x the next best). Other winners are a character digging a hole with his own words ("downplayed war crimes in his interview", "told a customer he got scammed out of 20k") or the system failing him (lag or seizure excuses, the judge blaming daylight savings).
3. **Write the hook so the premise is clear in under 10 words, with one concrete image.** Winners: "He freestyled himself into a corner…", "POV: cops call about the car you used in a robbery". Stop using tangled or run-on hooks. The flops were "When you say you smacked three guys and he heard you screamed" (9 views) and "POV: you trash talk the cop on the radio and he's standing right behind you" (10 views).
4. **"POV:" is fine but not a magic word.** It appears in most hooks and gives about median results (about 1.3–1.5k). The top two clips differ: one is a POV hook and one is a plain statement. Test more plain "He/She [did dumb thing]" hooks next to POV hooks. Keep one 💀 emoji. Don't stack emojis.
5. **Aim for 22–38 seconds.** On YouTube, almost every clip in that range beat the median (11 of 13 at roughly 1.3k or more). Clips over 40s were mixed: 4.5k, 3.5k and 1.7k, but also 232, 12 and 9 views. On TikTok, the opposite showed up weakly. The 47–49s clips were the only ones with solid views and like rates (1.0k at 4.6% likes, 1.0k at 5.7%, 360, 344). So treat the length range as a soft preference.
6. **Cut Cinna to proven formats only.** His 47–48s clips ("downed and crew drives off", "beg a stranger to drive you to the bathroom") did about 1.2–1.3k on YouTube and about 1k on TikTok. His gaslight and roof clip got 12 views, and the "rolling his R's" clip got 232 views. Cinna works when the story is a simple relatable-pain POV. It fails when the clip needs context.
7. **Stop picking vanillamace-style "weird situation introduces herself" clips for now.** The one clip got 12 views on YouTube and 438 on TikTok. One data point isn't enough to ban her, so retest once with a clearer premise.
8. **Webcam doesn't seem to be the deciding factor.** The only webcam-off clips were Cinna's weak "R's" clip (232 views) and Burn's brand-new clip (503 views at 1 hour old, which is promising). Webcam-on clips won and lost in equal measure. Prefer webcam-on when the funny moment is a facial reaction, but don't reject a great line because the cam is off.
9. **Watch Burn's hot-dog clip.** It had 503 views in its first hour, far faster than the others. If it keeps climbing, pick more kidnap and absurd-demand RP from Burn.
10. **Humor that worked is dialogue-driven deadpan, not screaming chaos.** Highest like rates on YouTube: freestyle (3.7%), 18 cops (1.5%), trick-or-treat cops (1.4%), lag excuse (1.1%). `chaos` and `reaction` tags alone didn't beat `funny_line` plus an authority figure (cop, judge, boss, interviewer).
11. **Fix the TikTok pipeline before changing content.** Seven clips with 0–1 views on TikTok got 9 to 10.7k on YouTube, for example the robbery clip (0 vs 10,667). They were posted at the same hour as the YouTube versions and were 237+ hours old. A uniform zero points to a muting, copyright, violence-flag or upload problem, not weak humor. Check those uploads. Don't draw content conclusions from TikTok zeros.
12. **Don't optimize posting hour yet.** Winners came from 09:00, 16:00 and 19:00, and flops from 11:00, 19:00 and 22:00. Hour is mixed up with clip quality and age. Post at varied times and test the same clip type at different hours next week.

Submit with the tool as JSON: {"picks": [{"id": int, "start": float, "end": float, "score": int, "hook_options": [str], "hook": str, "punch_text": str, "punch_at": float, "title": str, "caption": str, "tags": [str], "why": str}]}
